question: Given the clinical information already available (including ER, PR and HER2 status), does adding the H&E pathology images improve the four-class PAM50 prediction? How large is the gain, and how certain is the evidence?

objective.question: Given the clinical information already available (including ER, PR and HER2 status), does adding the H&E pathology images improve the four-class PAM50 prediction? How large is the gain, and how certain is the evidence?
objective.estimand: Paired difference in out-of-fold four-class PAM50 macro-F1 between image-plus-clinical and clinical-only models across identical labelled patients, with a patient-level 95% bootstrap confidence interval.
objective.target: Four-class PAM50 intrinsic subtype (LumA, LumB, Basal, Her2) per labelled patient.
allowed_inputs: Six clinical variables: age, stage, histological_type, and immunohistochemistry receptor statuses er, pr, her2
Patient mean-pooled H&E image features from five frozen encoders: UNI2-h, CONCH-Z, Virchow2, MUSK, H-Optimus-1
Tile-level H&E image features (up to 128 tiles per slide) from the five frozen encoders
Patient identifiers for pairing arms and keeping all slides and tiles of a patient within one split
Collection site column strictly for split grouping in the site-held-out sensitivity analysis, never as a predictor
Unlabelled patients' image and clinical features (n=259) strictly for fold-internal unsupervised representation learning, if used
forbidden_inputs: Collection site as a predictive model input
H&E image features in the clinical-only baseline arm
External TCGA molecular, clinical, or pathology annotations outside the provided dataset
Evaluation-fold features or labels during preprocessing, missing-value handling, dimensionality reduction, or model selection

forbidden_reasons.RNA expression or RNA-derived variables: PAM50 labels are computed from tumour RNA expression, so any RNA-derived input introduces direct target leakage and invalidates H&E evaluation.
forbidden_reasons.Collection site as a predictive model in: Site is a technical confounder correlated with subtype (Cramer's V = 0.21) and strongly encoded in slides, not biological morphology.
forbidden_reasons.H&E image features in the clinical-only: Contaminating the baseline arm with image features destroys the clinical-only reference required to estimate incremental H&E value.
forbidden_reasons.External TCGA molecular, clinical, or pa: Adding unprovided clinical or molecular variables alters the conditioned baseline and violates cohort scope.
forbidden_reasons.Evaluation-fold features or labels durin: Fitting transformations or selecting configurations across splits leaks held-out patients and inflates incremental gains in high dimensions.

required_comparators: floor_clinical: fully tuned clinical-only model using the six clinical variables on identical patients, folds, and missing-value handling
simple_reference: regularised logistic regression on clinical variables plus patient mean-pooled image features on identical folds
Site-held-out clinical-only versus image-plus-clinical comparison across the 19 collection sites to assess site confounding
objective.primary_metric: Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only) across repeated nested cross-validation, with a patient-level 95% bootstrap confidence interval
secondary_metrics: Paired out-of-fold multiclass log-loss difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only)
Paired out-of-fold macro one-vs-rest AUROC difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only)
Per-class recall differences for LumA, LumB, Basal, and Her2 (highlighting LumA, LumB, and minority Her2)
Site-held-out paired macro-F1 difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only) across the 19 collection sites
Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference against simple_reference on identical folds

acceptance_criteria.statement: Models use only allowed clinical and frozen H&E inputs, excluding RNA-derived variables and collection-site predictors.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Feature sets contain no forbidden inputs; the clinical-only arm uses only the six clinical variables while the multimodal arm adds only frozen H&E features.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Cross-validation splits partition strictly at the patient level, keeping all slides and tiles of each patient together.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Patient identifier sets across training and evaluation partitions are strictly disjoint in every outer fold, inner fold, and site-held-out split.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Clinical-only and image-plus-clinical arms evaluate identical labelled patients, folds, and fold-internal missing-value handling.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Out-of-fold predictions cover identical labelled patients and fold assignments, using identical explicit missing-level encoding and imputation fitted inside each training fold.

acceptance_criteria.statement: All encoder, fusion, dimensionality reduction, class-weighting, and hyperparameter choices occur strictly inside inner training folds.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Selection across encoders, tile versus mean levels, regularisation, and class weights uses inner-fold validation macro-F1 only, without accessing outer-fold evaluation patients.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Complex multimodal models are benchmarked directly against simple_reference on identical folds to guard against high-dimensional overfitting.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Complex tile-level or multi-encoder models are adopted over simple_reference only when their inner-fold macro-F1 exceeds the fold-matched simple_reference macro-F1.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Iterative optimisation for fitted models demonstrates stable training convergence within each cross-validation fold.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Logged per-fold training curves reach a stable trailing plateau where terminal loss updates are negligible relative to total fold loss reduction.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Primary paired macro-F1 difference is reported with a patient-level bootstrap confidence interval at the 95% level.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Resample labelled patients with replacement from paired out-of-fold predictions to compute the 95% confidence interval and compare bounds against zero difference.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Deliverables contain finite out-of-fold predictions for both arms, interval estimate, three-way conclusion, per-class changes, and site sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria.rule: All required outputs exist with finite values matching labelled cohort dimensions, valid class probabilities per patient, per-class recall changes, and site-held-out estimates.

conclusion_options: improves: Adding H&E images improves four-class PAM50 prediction over clinical variables (patient-level 95% bootstrap interval for paired macro-F1 difference lies strictly above zero).
insufficient evidence: Evidence is insufficient to establish a macro-F1 change from adding H&E images (patient-level 95% bootstrap interval contains zero).
worse: Adding H&E images worsens four-class PAM50 prediction relative to clinical variables alone (patient-level 95% bootstrap interval lies strictly below zero).
objective.conclusion_scope: Applies to incremental patient-level PAM50 prediction in this labelled TCGA-BRCA cohort; does not establish independent biological mechanisms, standalone H&E predictive value, or generalisability to external clinical cohorts.
objective.notes: IHC receptors belong in both arms. Use repeated nested CV (5 folds, 3 repeats), class weighting for minority Her2, and fold-fitted missingness levels. Historical 0.723 single-split score is not ground truth.

dataset_card.name: TCGA-BRCA diagnostic slides with clinical variables
dataset_card.description: Breast cancer patients with H&E whole-slide images and six clinical variables: age, stage, histological type, and the receptor statuses ER, PR and HER2 from immunohistochemistry. Images are represented by frozen pathology foundation models: five encoders, each giving one feature vector per tile (up to 128 tiles per slide, identical tile positions across encoders) and a mean-pooled vector per patient. The label is the PAM50 intrinsic subtype in four classes. Patients without a label still have images. Each patient has a collection site.

label_provenance.statement: PAM50 is computed from the tumour's RNA expression. Receptor status is correlated with PAM50 but is a separate clinical measurement and is not equivalent to it (immunohistochemistry surrogates disagree with PAM50 for a substantial share of tumours).
label_provenance.implication: No RNA-derived variable may be used as an input. Whether receptors may be used depends on the question asked: they are a legitimate baseline when the question is what images add to clinical information, and a forbidden shortcut when the question is what images alone contain.

dataset_card.scope_of_inference: incremental predictive value in this cohort; not an independent biological mechanism
dataset_card.how_predictions_are_scored: The evaluator re-runs every method inside its own repeated nested cross-validation on the labelled patients (outer 5 folds repeated 3 times, patient-level; any model or configuration choice happens only inside the training folds) and compares it with a fixed, fully tuned clinical-only model on the same patients and folds.

rulers.floor_clinical: clinical variables only, fixed and fully tuned by the evaluator; the gain is measured against it
rulers.simple_reference: clinical variables plus mean-pooled image features in a logistic regression; complex methods are compared with it
rulers.historical_reference: an earlier project's late fusion reached macro-F1 0.723 on a single 121-patient test split (not ground truth)

dataset_card.decision_rule: Primary metric: paired difference in macro-F1 (image plus clinical minus clinical only) with a patient-level bootstrap 95% interval. Conclusion, from the interval alone: "improves" if the lower bound is above 0; "insufficient evidence" if the interval contains 0; "worse" if the upper bound is below 0. Secondary: log-loss difference, one-vs-rest AUROC difference, per-class recall changes (LumA and LumB in particular), and a site-held-out sensitivity analysis. Both arms must use the same patients and the same missing-value handling.
dataset_card.deliverable: The estimated gain with its interval, the three-way conclusion, out-of-fold predictions for both arms, and the per-class changes.

difficulties.evidence: Class counts among 802 labelled patients: LumA 410, LumB 190, Basal 137, Her2 65. The smallest class is 8.1% of the cohort.
difficulties.implication: Use a class-balanced metric and class weighting; an unweighted model can score well while missing the smallest class entirely.

difficulties.evidence: Share of labelled patients without a definite value: er 4.7% (missing 4.5%), pr 5.1% (missing 4.6%), her2 31.8% (missing 15.3%), stage 2.6% (missing 2.6%), histological_type 0.1% (missing 0.1%), age 0.0% (missing 0.0%).
difficulties.implication: Handle missing values inside each training fold with an explicit missing level, identically in both comparison arms.

difficulties.evidence: 802 labelled patients against image features of 1536 (UNI2-h), 768 (CONCH-Z), 2560 (Virchow2), 1024 (MUSK), 1536 (H-Optimus-1) dimensions per encoder.
difficulties.implication: High-capacity image models overfit easily; regularise, reduce dimension inside folds, and require evidence of convergence and of a gain over a simple reference.

difficulties.evidence: Labelled patients come from 19 collection sites (largest 130 patients, 3 sites with fewer than 10). Image features (UNI2-h) identify the site of a patient with accuracy 0.89 against 0.17 for always guessing the largest site; site and class are associated (Cramer's V = 0.21).
difficulties.implication: Part of an image-based gain may come from site signatures; a site-held-out sensitivity analysis should accompany the main estimate.

difficulties.evidence: PAM50 is computed from the tumour's RNA expression. Receptor status is correlated with PAM50 but is a separate clinical measurement and is not equivalent to it (immunohistochemistry surrogates disagree with PAM50 for a substantial share of tumours).
difficulties.implication: No RNA-derived variable may be used as an input. Whether receptors may be used depends on the question asked: they are a legitimate baseline when the question is what images add to clinical information, and a forbidden shortcut when the question is what images alone contain.

difficulties.evidence: 46 labelled patients have more than one slide; tiles per patient range from 6 to 471 (median 124).
difficulties.implication: The patient is the unit of analysis: all slides and tiles of a patient must stay on the same side of every split.

difficulties.evidence: Clinical variables alone reach macro-F1 0.576 in 5-fold cross-validation; recall by class: LumA 0.54, LumB 0.54, Basal 0.82, Her2 0.52. The weakest class is Her2.
difficulties.implication: The question is about what images add to this baseline, so the clinical arm must be tuned as carefully as the image arm and evaluated on the same patients.

difficulties.evidence: For a simple image-plus-clinical model against clinical only, the paired macro-F1 difference has a bootstrap standard error of 0.021 with one 5-fold split of 802 patients. The smallest difference detectable with 80% power is about 0.059.
difficulties.implication: Gains of a few points cannot be established from one split; use repeated cross-validation and report an interval, not only a point estimate.

difficulties.evidence: 5 image encoders are available, each usable at tile or patient level with several fusion strategies.
difficulties.implication: Choosing the best of many configurations on the evaluation folds inflates the reported gain; selection must be nested or counted.

P1.name: Nested PCA-Reduced Patient-Mean Logistic Fusion
P1.summary: This simple reference plan tests whether mean-pooled H&E features improve four-class PAM50 prediction over the six clinical covariates. Within repeated patient-level nested cross-validation, each fold fits identical missing-level clinical encodings, reduces one inner-selected encoder via PCA, and trains class-balanced logistic regression paired with a tuned clinical-only model. A site-held-out analysis checks site confounding. The paired bootstrap 95% interval for macro-F1 difference determines whether global morphology improves, worsens, or shows insufficient evidence.
preprocessing: Verify patient-level alignment across all 802 labelled patients (keeping multi-slide patients pooled into their single patient-mean vector per encoder), exclude the 259 unlabelled patients from supervised splits, and exclude all RNA-derived variables and collection site from predictor matrices.

Inside each inner, outer, and site-held-out training fold, impute age with the training-fold median and z-score standardise it; one-hot encode stage, histological_type, er, pr, and her2 using training-fold categories plus an explicit 'Missing' category level, sharing the exact encoded clinical matrix between clinical_only and patient_mean_logreg.

Inside each training fold, z-score standardise the candidate encoder's patient-mean H&E vector using training-fold mean and SD, fit PCA strictly on training-fold patients to retain n_pca components, z-score standardise the resulting PC scores using training-fold SDs, and concatenate with the clinical features.
Run sanity checks before scoring confirming disjoint patient IDs across splits, identical patient ordering across both arms, and non-trivial behaviour of the tuned clinical_only comparator.

training.convergence_check: Record per-iteration multinomial cross-entropy loss and gradient norm in every fold; confirm optimisation converges prior to max_epochs with trailing relative loss change below 1e-5.

tuning.tie_rule: Treat inner-fold macro-F1 differences smaller than 0.005 as ties and select the most parsimonious configuration (smaller n_pca, smaller C).

validation.oof_aggregation: Evaluate paired out-of-fold predictions on identical splits across the 3 repeats, compute repeat-averaged patient-level class probabilities for the 802 patients, and draw 10,000 patient-level bootstrap resamples with replacement to form the paired 95% confidence interval.
validation.site_sensitivity: Run grouped leave-one-site-out cross-validation across all 19 collection sites (using site strictly as split group, never as a feature) with 3-fold patient-level inner CV inside training sites for both clinical_only and patient_mean_logreg.

metrics: Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only) across repeated nested CV with a patient-level 95% bootstrap confidence interval
Paired out-of-fold multiclass log-loss difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only)
Paired out-of-fold macro one-vs-rest AUROC difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only)
Per-class recall differences for LumA, LumB, Basal, and Her2
Site-held-out paired macro-F1 difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only) across the 19 collection sites
P1.allowed_conclusions: Conclude 'improves' if the 95% patient-level bootstrap confidence interval for paired macro-F1 difference lies strictly above zero, 'worse' if strictly below zero, and 'insufficient evidence' if it contains zero; qualify potential site confounding using the 19-site held-out difference and restrict scope to incremental linear patient-mean H&E prediction in this TCGA-BRCA cohort.

diversity.method: early concatenation with nested encoder/PCA grid selection

P1.rationale: Foundation embeddings risk overfitting on 802 imbalanced patients alongside informative receptor covariates. Fold-internal PCA with class-balanced L2 logistic regression provides a low-variance linear benchmark under nested encoder selection. Complex tile-level or non-linear models are justified only if they outperform this reference on identical folds.

P2.name: Residual Logit-Offset Dual-Encoder Tile Attention MIL
P2.summary: Each patient is represented by six clinical covariates and a multi-slide bag of aligned UNI2-h and CONCH-Z tile embeddings compressed via fold-internal PCA. A tuned, class-balanced clinical baseline provides frozen log-odds offsets, and a zero-initialised gated-attention MIL network learns strictly the residual PAM50 signal from H&E tiles. Repeated nested patient-level cross-validation pairs predictions against clinical-only and simple-reference comparators, accompanied by leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis. The 95% patient-bootstrap interval on paired macro-F1 difference determines whether H&E images improve, leave uncertain, or worsen cohort PAM50 prediction.
preprocessing: Pool all diagnostic slides and tiles of each patient into a single patient-level bag and verify strictly disjoint patient IDs across all outer, inner, and site-held-out splits ( excluding RNA variables and never using site as a predictor).

Inside each training fold, encode stage, histological_type, er, pr, and her2 via one-hot encoding with an explicit missing/indeterminate category, and median-impute plus z-score age using training-fold statistics identically across clinical-only, simple-reference, and residual-offset arms.

Inside each training fold, fit the tuned class-balanced clinical_only comparator (floor_clinical); generate internal out-of-fold clinical log-odds on training patients as de-overfitted training offsets, and use the fold-refitted floor_clinical log-odds on held-out patients, verifying epoch-0 zero-initialised predictions exactly match floor_clinical.

Inside each training fold, L2-normalise and z-score UNI2-h (1536d) and CONCH-Z (768d) tile features separately using training-fold tile statistics, concatenate aligned per-tile vectors (2304d), and fit 128-component randomised PCA on training-fold tiles only before projecting patient bags.

training.convergence_check: Log per-epoch training and inner-validation weighted cross-entropy loss per fold; confirm trailing 5-epoch absolute loss change prior to checkpoint is under 1% of total loss reduction (or gradient norm plateaued near zero when residual signal is negligible).
training.selection_tie_breaker: Measure inner-fold macro-F1 spread across resamples; treat grid differences within one standard error as ties and select the higher-regularisation configuration; adopt over fold-matched simple_reference only when inner-fold macro-F1 exceeds simple_reference (A5).

P2.rationale: Freezing out-of-fold clinical logits with a zero-initialised residual head protects the strong clinical baseline (D7) against high-dimensional overfitting (D3), focusing image capacity on LumA/LumB separation and missing-HER2 cases (D2). Tile attention across patient slides (D6) captures focal proliferative and minority Her2 morphology (D1).

P3.name: Unlabelled-PCA Five-Encoder Gated FiLM Hierarchical Network
P3.summary: We fuse patient-pooled features from all five vision and vision-language pathology encoders with the six clinical variables. Within each training fold, per-encoder PCA subspaces are fitted on training plus 259 unlabelled patients, then integrated through learned encoder gating, clinical FiLM conditioning, and a hierarchical head separating coarse subtypes before resolving LumA versus LumB. Repeated nested cross-validation compares predictions against tuned clinical, simple logistic, and site-excluded baselines. A paired patient bootstrap interval decides whether H&E images improve PAM50 classification.
preprocessing: Pool all tiles across all slides of each patient into one patient-level mean feature vector per encoder (UNI2-h, CONCH-Z, Virchow2, MUSK, H-Optimus-1), keeping all data of a patient within the same split.

Inside each inner and outer training fold, one-hot encode stage, histological_type, er, pr, and her2 with an explicit missing/indeterminate level (capturing 31.8% indefinite her2) and standardize age using training-fold statistics (median-imputed if missing), identically across floor_clinical, simple_reference, and multimodal arms.

Inside each inner and outer training fold, standardize and fit 64-component whitened PCA independently for each of the five encoders using training-fold labelled patients combined with the 259 unlabelled patients (excluding unlabelled patients from the held-out site during site-held-out evaluation), without accessing evaluation-fold patients or labels.
Verify strict exclusion of RNA-derived variables and collection site from all model feature matrices.

training.convergence_check: Log per-fold training and inner-validation loss curves; verify trailing 5-epoch mean loss update is under 1% of total fold loss reduction before checkpoint adoption.

validation.tie_rule: Select on inner-fold validation macro-F1; prefer stronger regularisation or flat head when differences lie within 1 seed-ensemble standard error, and adopt complex model over fold-matched simple_reference on outer folds only when inner-fold macro-F1 exceeds simple_reference.
validation.site_sensitivity: 19-fold leave-one-site-out nested cross-validation grouped by site (site never used as predictor; held-out site excluded from unlabelled PCA pool), evaluating pooled out-of-site paired predictions across all 802 labelled patients.

Clinical FiLM reweights morphology when HER2 is indefinite (D2), and hierarchical classification targets minority Her2 plus LumA versus LumB confusion (D1, D7).

P4.name: Multi-Scale Morphological-Prototype and Boosted-Tree Super-Learner
P4.summary: Each patient's slides are summarised by compositional tile-prototype histograms (Virchow2, H-Optimus-1) and PCA-compressed global embeddings (H-Optimus-1, MUSK, CONCH-Z), integrated with clinical covariates via nested probability stacking. Within each training fold, a regularised logistic meta-learner blends out-of-fold probabilities from a clinical-only anchor, linear and boosted-tree prototype classifiers, and multi-encoder gradient boosting, benchmarked against the simple reference. Paired macro-F1 differences across repeated patient-level cross-validation and site-held-out splits with a 95% bootstrap interval determine whether H&E images improve PAM50 prediction.
preprocessing: Pool all slides and tiles per patient_id (handling 46 multi-slide patients and bag sizes of 6-471 tiles) into one patient bag before splitting; verify disjoint patient_id sets across all outer, inner, and site splits, excluding site and any RNA-derived variables from predictors.

Inside each training fold, apply identical clinical preprocessing to floor_clinical, simple_reference, and multimodal arms: median-impute and z-score age on labelled training patients, and one-hot encode stage, histological_type, er, pr, and her2 with explicit missing/indefinite levels.

Using training-fold labelled patients plus the 259 unlabelled patients (never evaluation-fold patients), L2-normalise embeddings, fit 64-dim tile PCA on Virchow2 and H-Optimus-1 before k-means clustering to compute bag-size-invariant prototype-share histograms summing to 1, and fit concatenated patient-mean PCA across H-Optimus-1, MUSK, and CONCH-Z.

Compute inverse-prevalence balanced sample weights strictly from training-fold PAM50 class counts and log iterative convergence curves (k-means centroid shift, per-iteration boosting deviance, and L-BFGS meta-learner loss) until terminal updates plateau below 1% of total fold loss reduction.

tuning.tie_rule: Measure selection spread across inner folds and 2 seeds; break differences within spread (<0.005 macro-F1) toward smaller n_prototypes/n_pca and stronger meta weight_decay, and adopt over simple_reference only when inner-fold macro-F1 strictly exceeds fold-matched simple_reference (A5).

P4.rationale: Quantising tiles into bag-size-invariant prototype proportions preserves focal LumA/LumB heterogeneity while compressing high-dimensional features and dampening continuous stain shifts (D3, D4, D6). Boosted trees model non-linear interactions with missing HER2 (D2), while clinical-anchored probability stacking down-weights overfitted image branches (D7, D9).

P5.name: Clinical-Query Cross-Attention Vision-Language Tile Transformer
P5.summary: Each patient's H&E tiles from compact vision-language encoders (CONCH-Z, MUSK) pass through a learned linear bottleneck and shallow tile transformer, then undergo cross-attention queried by the six clinical variables including explicit missing receptor states. Conditioning tile selection on clinical status focuses spatial attention on invasive subregions relevant to LumA versus LumB separation or missing HER2 cases. Paired 5x3 nested cross-validation, 19-site held-out testing, and a 95% patient bootstrap interval quantify incremental PAM50 value.
preprocessing: Pool all diagnostic slide tiles per patient (up to 128 tiles per slide) into a single patient bag while keeping patient IDs strictly disjoint across every outer, inner, and site-held-out split; exclude all RNA-derived variables and exclude collection site from predictive inputs (A1, A2, D6).

Inside each training fold identically for floor_clinical, simple_reference, and conditional_fusion arms, z-score standardise age using training-fold mean/SD and one-hot encode stage, histological_type, er, pr, and her2 with explicit Missing and Equivocal/Indeterminate levels so evaluation-fold unseen states map without leakage (A3, D2).

Inside each training fold, L2-normalise frozen CONCH-Z (768-d) and MUSK (1024-d) tile embeddings and standardise per channel using training-fold statistics only, replacing unsupervised PCA with an end-to-end regularised linear projection so stain- and site-dominated variance axes do not discard subtype morphology (D3, D4).

Run a pre-evaluation sanity audit verifying floor_clinical accesses only the six clinical covariates, achieves non-zero recall on minority Her2 under class weighting, and matches patient/fold indexing of simple_reference (K7, K8).

training.convergence_check: Log per-epoch training and inner-validation loss curves for every fold; require trailing 5-epoch mean loss update to be under 2% of total fold loss reduction before scoring, extending up to 80 epochs if plateau is not reached (A6, K3).

P6.name: Semi-Supervised Split-Bag Pre-Adapted Gigapixel Tile MIL
P6.summary: We represent each patient by six clinical variables (with explicit missing levels) and Virchow2 plus H-Optimus-1 tile bags. Inside every fold, we apply PCA and pretrain a multihead attention aggregator via self-supervised split-bag agreement across training and 259 unlabelled patients before balanced multimodal fine-tuning. Repeated nested patient cross-validation, inner benchmarking against simple_reference, and a 19-site audit control overfitting and confounding. The paired 95% bootstrap macro-F1 interval determines whether H&E improves PAM50 prediction.
preprocessing: Pool all slides and up to 128 aligned tiles per slide into one bag per patient ID (keeping all slides of the 46 multi-slide patients together); strip any RNA-derived columns and exclude collection site from all model inputs (A1, A2, D5, D6).

Inside each training split (inner, outer, and site-held-out), fit identical clinical transformations for floor_clinical, simple_reference, and ssl_preadapted_mil: z-score age using training-split statistics and one-hot encode stage, histological_type, er, pr, and her2 with an explicit missing_or_indeterminate level (A3, D2).

Inside each training split, L2-normalise tile vectors per encoder and fit randomized PCA (dim=128) strictly on tiles from that split's labelled training patients plus the 259 unlabelled patients, projecting validation tiles without accessing held-out patients or labels (A4, D3).
Verify baseline sanity and strict modality isolation on a pilot split for floor_clinical and simple_reference prior to full nested cross-validation execution (K8).

training.convergence_criterion: Record per-epoch Stage-1 consistency loss and Stage-2 class-balanced cross-entropy loss in every fold; confirm trailing 5-epoch mean loss change is <2% of total fold loss reduction before reading scores (A6, K3).

validation.tie_and_simplicity_rule: Treat inner-fold macro-F1 differences <0.005 as ties in favour of stronger regularisation (K1); adopt ssl_preadapted_mil over fold-matched simple_reference in outer fold only when inner-fold macro-F1 strictly exceeds simple_reference (A5), while also archiving ungated ssl_preadapted_mil OOF predictions.
validation.site_held_out_sensitivity: 19-split Leave-One-Site-Out cross-validation grouped strictly by collection site (never using site as a predictor), pooling out-of-site predictions across all 802 labelled patients to compute paired macro-F1 difference against site-held-out floor_clinical (D4, K9).
validation.bootstrap_details: 10,000 patient-level cluster bootstrap resamples of the 802 labelled patients across paired repeat-wise out-of-fold predictions to compute the 95% confidence interval (A7, D8).

plans.name: Nested Single-Encoder Patient-Mean Balanced Logistic Reference
plans.summary: This simple reference estimates how much PAM50 subtype information is linearly recoverable from patient-mean H&E features alone, excluding all clinical, receptor, RNA, and site variables. Within repeated nested patient-level cross-validation, inner folds select a single foundation encoder, PCA rank, and L2 penalty for class-weighted multinomial logistic regression, benchmarked against majority-class and class-prior null baselines. Parallel site-held-out cross-validation across 19 sites audits institutional confounding, establishing the required linear benchmark and testing broad, partial, or site-confounded predictability.
preprocessing: Exclude all forbidden clinical, immunohistochemistry receptor (er, pr, her2), histological_type, age, stage, RNA-derived, and site variables from predictor matrices; assert zero non-image features before fitting.

Restrict supervised modelling and scoring to the 802 PAM50-labelled patients (excluding the 259 unlabelled patients), pooling multi-slide patients into a single tile-count-weighted patient-mean embedding per encoder so every patient is one row.

Within each inner and outer training fold independently, apply feature-wise z-score standardisation followed by truncated SVD PCA (n_pca <= 256, strictly below inner-fold sample size ~427) and transform held-out patients using training-fold parameters only.

Compute inverse-frequency balanced class weights strictly from training-fold subtype counts (LumA, LumB, Basal, Her2) and fit training-fold majority-class and stratified class-prior null baselines on identical fold assignments.
Retain collection site (19 groups) strictly as an external split-grouping index for the secondary site-held-out cross-validation sensitivity audit.

Within nested training folds, per-encoder tile features are standardized and PCA-compressed before a neural network performs per-tile encoder fusion and gated-attention pooling to predict class-weighted PAM50 subtypes. Evaluation uses repeated nested patient-level and site-held-out cross-validation against null baselines and the patient-mean logistic reference. new_components.name: shared_private_poe_vib
new_components.description: Computes a semi-supervised multi-view Shared-Private Product-of-Experts Variational Information Bottleneck across M=5 patient-level encoder vectors (each 256-dim fold-whitened PCA). Inputs: 5 aligned patient vectors for labelled and unlabelled training-fold patients plus integer PAM50 labels for labelled training patients only (5 vectors per held-out labelled patient at inference). Architecture: M view-specific 2-layer LayerNorm-GELU-Dropout MLPs map each view m to shared diagonal Gaussian posterior parameters (mu_m, clamp(logvar_m, -6, 6)) in R^{shared_dim} and deterministic private latents z_priv_m in R^{private_dim}. Closed-form precision-weighted Product-of-Experts combines active views S with prior N(0,I): prec_poe = 1 + sum_{m in S} exp(-logvar_m), mu_poe = prec_poe^{-1} sum_{m in S} exp(-logvar_m)*mu_m. View decoders reconstruct all M views from [z_shared, z_priv_m] (substituting zero private vector for masked views m not in S). A cosine-normalized linear head with learnable scale maps z_shared (using deterministic mu_poe at test time) to 4 class scores f(z). Training: AdamW on mixed labelled+unlabelled mini-batches with random view masking (p=0.3, keeping >=2 views) and labelled latent mixup, minimizing logit-adjusted cross-entropy CE(f(z) + tau*log(pi_train), y) on labelled samples plus rec_weight*MSE across all M views, linearly warmed beta_kl*KL(q_poe||N(0,I)), and orth_weight*sum(||z_shared^T z_priv_m||_F^2 + 0.1*||z_priv_m||_2^2) on all training+unlabelled samples. After convergence, fits scalar temperature T>0 (inner-val NLL) for calibrated probabilities p_hat = softmax((f(mu_poe)+log(pi_train))/T) and simplex weights alpha in Delta^3 (coordinate ascent on inner-val macro-F1) for discrete predictions argmax_c(alpha_c * p_hat_c), averaging p_hat across n_seeds_ensemble seeds. Outputs: calibrated 4-class probabilities, macro-F1-calibrated class predictions, consensus embeddings, and epoch loss/metric curves.

new_components.name: clinical_prior_poe_vib
new_components.description: Computes: A semi-supervised Clinical-Prior Variational Information Bottleneck with analytical Bayesian Product-of-Experts (PoE) precision gating. A clinical MLP maps fold-encoded clinical covariates c to a diagonal Gaussian prior N(mu_c, sigma_c^2). A visual branch applies gated attention over within-patient centered tile residuals concatenated with global bag mean and residual dispersion (SD, interdecile range) to output visual Gaussian parameters (mu_x, sigma_x^2) with clamped log-variance [-3.0, 1.4] and high-variance initialization so initial visual precision Lambda_x is near zero. Closed-form PoE sets Lambda_cx = Lambda_c + Lambda_x and mu_cx = mu_c + (Lambda_x / Lambda_cx) * (mu_x - mu_c), updating clinical representations selectively on uncertain dimensions. Inputs: Fold-encoded clinical matrix, 192-dim global mean, 384-dim residual dispersion stats, and 192-dim within-patient residual tile bags for labelled fold-train and 259 unlabelled patients. Outputs: Four-class PAM50 probabilities from deterministic MAP latent mu_cx (3-seed outer ensemble), per-patient incremental KL divergence, and epoch loss traces. Training: AdamW on balanced PAM50 cross-entropy from reparameterized z_cx plus clinical_prior_sup_weight balanced PAM50 loss on z_c (labelled train), beta_kl closed-form KL(q(z|c,x) || p(z|c)) with 20-epoch linear warmup, and aux_clinical_weight masked clinical-attribute reconstruction from mu_x across fold-train and unlabelled patients.
